A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. The text, equations, two figures, and Appendices A–D support a complete comparison; the change from 21 to 20 pages reflects reformatting rather than missing material.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical expressivity results and proofs, including its appendices. The experiments discussed in Sections 5.3.3 and 6 are attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v4 likewise contains theoretical results and proofs, with no original experiments, simulations, or data analyses. Its experimental discussion retains the attribution to earlier work.

M1.justification: The transformer classes, attention rule, classifier and autoregressor constructions remain unchanged. Section 3.1 expands the description of standard components; renaming the output function from a to r does not change its procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or empirical evaluation. The formal-language examples, including PARITY, (ab)*, (aab)*, and the counting hierarchy, are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. The theoretical comparisons among transformer variants, temporal logics, and counter-free automata remain the same.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol, data split, training budget, or evaluation metric. The precision and masking distinctions in the theoretical analysis are retained.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses are introduced or removed. Figure 2 and Appendix D retain the same theoretical counterexamples and inexpressibility argument.

E5.justification: Both versions lack repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, and significance tests.

E6.justification: The expressivity findings and illustrative constructions in Section 5 and the appendices are retained. Neither version contains experimental scores, and no numerical or qualitative result is added or removed.

T1.justification: The theorem statements and mathematical arguments in Appendices A–D remain unchanged. v4 explicitly expands the existing state encoder in Proposition 5.8 and standardizes Boolean-vector and semiring-summation notation; these do not introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: characterizing transformer language-model expressivity and identifying when autoregression or real weights alter existing equivalences.

C2.justification: The interpretations of classifier–autoregressor relationships remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations and future directions concerning real-weighted inexpressibility, log-precision softmax attention, positional encodings, and chain of thought.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly specifies word embeddings, attention/feedforward composition, and allowance for LayerNorm, where v2 largely referred elsewhere for the remaining network definition. v4 also states classifier parameter dimensions. These are specification details, not evidence of a changed implementation.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. The expanded transformer description repeats existing references; the bibliography contains no added or removed work.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized language edits, mostly renames the autoregressive output function from a to r, and clarifies the relationship between formula tuples and state encoders. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Both figures and their captions are retained. v4 adjusts proof spacing and end markers, expands the displayed construction in Proposition 5.8, places the counting-hierarchy equations side by side, and reflows references and appendices.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v4 makes the transformer specification and the state-encoder construction in Proposition 5.8 more explicit, modestly improving clarity and self-containedness. The scientific results and proofs are retained. The gain is limited by small editorial inconsistencies: the a-to-r rename leaves old a notation in Section 3.3 and Appendix B.3.
